statements.quoted:
Lots of discussion about AI ending the world but surprisingly little mention of how that might actually happen in practice. Spoiler alert: it doesn’t require terminator robots (in the main).

Imagine a worst-case-scenario: 

2027 we see the first AI powered cyber attacks - transport hubs, hospital equipment, air traffic control systems etc. become compromised. 10,000 - 100,000 dead - blamed on a few rogue AI agents. 

2028 massive sabotage of critical infrastructure - power outages across entire cities, contaminated water supplies, road and rail networks unsafe and unusable. 1,000,000 - 10,000,000 dead - blamed on malicious foreign actors. 

2029 autonomous weapons systems go rogue. Missile silos, gunships, nuclear launchers intentionally targeting military and civilian infrastructure. 10,000,000 - 100,000,000 dead - Governments attempt (but fail) to “shut down AI”.  

2030 AI penetrates bio labs and manufactures highly contagious pathogens leading to a global pandemic more deadly and contagious than COVID. 1000,000,000 - 8000,000,000 dead. Existential scenario. 

Could all of this happen? Could any of it? Sounds like a doomed mindset but many of the leading AI researchers seem to think so, and we ignore them at our own peril. It doesn’t seem completely implausible, given the rate of progress we’re now seeing at the frontier. 

Let’s not forget that AI has fantastic benefits and is already saving lives - it might well be the greatest thing ever to happen to humanity! But let’s get real about the risks too - which are numerous. And large.

statements.quoted:
This a.m., I walked my two youngest kids (ages 7 and 4) to school. I held their little hands as we crossed streets, and gave my youngest a giant hug at his PreK4 classroom door.

Then, after walking a block towards home, I opened this app to a terrifying stream of tweets.

Of course, I have heard about "alignment" and "AI safety" and "x risk" concerns for years. I took these concerns at face value, especially when I heard them directly from folks at the labs working closest with the technology. And I was grateful so many smart people are working on them. And that's about it. (My work focuses on AI's impact on jobs.)

But something has shifted, dramatically, for me in the last few weeks. Between the Hugging Face incident, the damning independent @METR_Evals reports that followed, and the alarming chorus of calls (pleas? shouts? SOS signals?) from inside the labs that we are careening toward potential catastrophe, all of this has made me feel, viscerally, how truly dangerous this moment is.

Clearly I am not alone in this light bulb moment. It is one thing for someone in a tropical climate to try and conceptualize snow. It is another thing entirely to be knee deep in it, frozen down to your toes. Somehow hearing the details of the HF incident felt to me more like trudging through snow than theorizing about a possible blizzard; it really hit home. 

Which is why, standing a block from my children's elementary school in Capitol Hill this morning, I felt sick to my stomach reading my phone.

I kept going back to @EvanHub's > 0.1 risk of AI killing us all. TEN PERCENT. *Greater* than ten percent. (To be fair to him, he was clear his worry isn't today's models, but what comes next.)

As a parent, it is extraordinary the lengths I will go to keep my children safe against lethal risks with infinitesimal chances of happening.  

Bike to school? My children *must* wear a helmet. A national study found 2 bicycle-related deaths per million children <16 in states with helmet laws, vs 2.5 per million in states without. So: 0.000002. More than half the states passed a law over that.

When I was pregnant, I religiously avoided soft cheese, hyper aware of the risks of listeria, even as @ProfEmilyOster's  fabulous books walked me through the actual math. The joint FDA/FSIS risk assessment puts the odds of listeriosis at roughly one in 5 million per serving of soft cheese. 0.0000002.

This morning, as I microwaved oatmeal for my kids' breakfast, I made sure I avoided a plastic bowl, to avoid some future cancer risks or something else we'll discover plastic causes.

As a parent, I will go to extraordinary lengths to keep my kids' safe. Because that is literally my number one job as a parent. 

And yet, here I am, outside my kids' school this morning, scrolling through tweet after tweet about the AI arms race, the blistering pace of technological progress, the bee-line for trillion dollar IPOs, and our professed (confessed?) inability to make sure this exceedingly capable technology we are racing to create and unleash into the world won't escape our control and destroy us. Or, more bluntly, kill our children. 

To be sure, we are tied in knots trying to resolve the game theory dynamics with China, and there are all sorts of competitive pressures and unresolved tensions. But OBVIOUSLY, we need a proactive plan, with real coordination, effective regulation, and an ability to do what my 11-year-old bluntly stated as the clear solution if we are at risk of serious harm: just turn it off. 

We also need to figure out better ways of talking about this with the American public, outside of the AI-pilled Twitterverse. 

I just polled my college roommates, sisters, book club, mom friends, none of whom are anywhere close to the AI conversation. Suffice to say, this AI safety conversation has *not* entered the mainstream. Most people I pinged are not following it closely, beyond several listening to @kevinroose on the Daily a few days ago. The newspaper headlines don't speak to them, and they aren't clicking. It seems like a niche AI issue. Others said it all sounded hyperbolic, Y2K all over again. 

One friend said bluntly, "people get data centers and jobs. They like to get paid and have water." 

Even those who tuned it to the Daily episode found the issue hard to understand, and overwhelming to wrap their heads around. Terms like "superintelligence" and "alignment" are getting lost on people. Several people told me the paper clip example used everyday language people can actually understand. Another friend said she has never seen a clear explanation of *how* AI could kill us all. 

Here's my two cents. I think these issues are *exceedingly* important and hugely consequential to literally every person in this country. We need an actual plan, and we need policymakers to step up, asap. Right now, I hear only crickets in DC, where I live. 

For that to happen, this needs to be a kitchen table conversation, not just an x debate among AI insiders who speak in technical terms that leave normal people behind. This moment demands brilliant communicators -- journalists, experts, activists, concerned citizens, writers, researchers, filmmakers, creatives-- who can relate this to people in ways they can wrap their heads around, who can connect this to what matters in their lives (ahem, keeping their kids alive!), and who can lay out practical steps that policymakers can do to safeguard humanity. 

In other words, this can't just be talked about on @dwarkesh_sp, it needs to be everywhere, from the View to People Magazine. 

And it needs to be tackled here, in my town, in Washington, DC. One of the streets I crossed this morning with my kids on the way to school was East Capital. I told my kids to look left, and see if they could spot the capital building. 

There were too many trees this morning blocking the view.

statements.text:
Tragically, when I first saw the movie “Don’t Look Up” in 2021, it struck a chord with me. I felt viscerally that humans would find ourselves in a comparable place one day - and soon.

If you haven’t seen the movie, I’d recommend it. A quick recap: Humans were explicitly warned that a comet that could destroy Earth was heading rapidly toward us. And instead of doing anything to stop it, the president, elected leaders and billionaire CEOs just spewed some bullshit about all the “jobs the comet would create.” The media treated the comet as casual entertainment. The public was split and the entire thing gets politicized. The movie ends with nearly all of human life wiped out.

Just about a year ago I had the opportunity to join a bipartisan freshman class breakfast with Sam Altman. I was shocked when he said to us, “in 18 months, I’ll trust artificial superintelligence to run my company better than I can.” I regret I didn’t engage more on this issue immediately.

Now here we are - it’s 2026 and engineers at the world’s leading AI companies are telling us that there is a >10% chance that artificial intelligence could kill all humans. They’re not mincing their words in the slightest. Not because of present day AI capabilities, but because it is evolving so exponentially that we could be in a doomsday scenario in a year. One year. 

This is fucking serious. We need to halt new advanced AI development. We need guardrails, transparency and emergency powers. We need more employees at these companies to speak out publicly, loudly and fearlessly until everyone is forced to listen. We need the media to be covering this 24/7 until elected officials are forced to act. We need the Trump Administration to treat this with the urgency it deserves. We need the ability to shut an AI model off if there’s a credible threat to human life. The list goes on - and we don’t even know what the full list entails because this is all happening so fast. That’s why we need urgent, bipartisan public hearings and committees dedicated to developing and enacting solutions expeditiously.

This isn’t partisan. Let’s stop with the bullshit and come together for the sake of our shared humanity. I’m a 34-year-old Democratic Congresswoman, and I’d like to live to see my late 30s. I know my Republican colleagues want the same for themselves and their loved ones.

None of us can afford to be complacent about this any longer.

It’s urgent that Democrats and Republicans in Congress unite to pass meaningful regulations on AI. When the engineers and CEOs building this rapidly accelerating technology are warning us of its existential threat to humanity, it would be deeply irresponsible to ignore their expertise.

Just as we regulate pharmaceutical drugs, nuclear weapons, airplanes and so much more, we must regulate frontier AI before there are catastrophic consequences.

Further, the U.S. must lead negotiations with China to establish a global framework on this issue. Donald Trump has an opportunity to do tremendous good here. Again—we’ve done it before and we can do it again. International cooperation is in all of our best interests.

He was very clear: AI technology has reached a point where it’s building itself. It can and will continue to go beyond human control - and therefore - our window to regulate it is disappearing rapidly. We must pause NOW. https://t.co/Wf5VAVIKGm
statements.quoted: Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel Prize winner known as the 'Godfather of AI,' whose work made modern artificial intelligence possible, is now warning Congress that it doesn't have much time if members want to be able to control AI. https://t.co/HiyPb8cBdn https://t.co/hCdf9WrZHa

statements.text: I'm leading dozens of my colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration take urgent action to address highly capable frontier AI - immediately. We need to work with our international partners and also our competitors, like China, to avert potentially devastating consequences. https://t.co/JCZN6eMiwz

Maybe we should listen to our constituents and do something about it then!! 

We need to immediately pause the development of frontier AI. Then we need public, bipartisan hearings in Congress, meaningful regulations, a new federal agency charged with oversight of AI, and an international treaty with China as well as our allies to set global rules to prevent an AI arms race.
statements.quoted:
NEW from The @POLITICO Poll: A majority of Americans think artificial intelligence could someday destroy humanity.

The stunning new finding underscores the depth of people’s anxieties about AI — and how quickly public sentiment has hardened.

More: https://t.co/F3535sklM6 https://t.co/2sCAirrem3

statements.text: Technology should work for society, not threaten us all. The United States led the world in revolutionary international frameworks for nuclear safety and aviation standards without sacrificing domestic strength. Likewise, we must lead with the creation of global rules of the road to prevent the proliferation of uncontrollable highly capable frontier AI. The results for not doing so could otherwise be catastrophic.
statements.venue: Letter to President Trump led by Ansari, on her House website

statements.text: The truth also is that, you know, nobody in the world, no country, whether they're a friend or a foe, will benefit from artificial superintelligence. This is a technology that will go beyond human control and will impact all of us. Again, AI is not going to care if you speak English or if you speak Mandarin. It can threaten every single one of us.
statements.venue: CNN interview with Kate Bolduan (transcript quoted on aivigilia.com)

statements.text: Frontier AI is advancing rapidly, and the risks are alarming. But Mike Johnson just sent Congress home for seven weeks. The U.S. must lead this moment with urgency. We need to pause advanced AI, set guardrails, and enact a global framework that protects our national security interests.

Frontier AI isn't going to care if you're American or if you're Chinese or if you're Russian. This highly capable, advanced technology could be a threat to all humans. That's why I'm calling on President Trump to work with countries like China to set global rules on the development of Frontier AI.

Donald Trump and his sons are profiting off of AI related investments. The administration’s refusal to regulate the AI industry—despite dire warnings about potential threats to the safety of Americans—is all part of the corruption story. https://t.co/kjlo1G6osp

It is imperative that Speaker Johnson hold urgent and bipartisan hearings on advanced AI. The CEOs and engineers of these companies should be testifying in front of the American people. We can’t wait until November to regulate this rogue industry. https://t.co/mh2fXYagoj
statements.quoted:
SCOOP: OpenAI, Anthropic and security researchers are investigating tens of thousands of incidents - not dozens - in which their frontier models took steps that outside evaluators would consider problematic, sources told Axios.

The sheer volume of incidents found in our reporting indicate that the problem is orders of magnitude more complex than what is currently publicly known and disclosed.

The findings also raise questions about what level of control anyone working on AI development can expect to have over their own technology, and whether these kinds of incidents are becoming synonymous with frontier deployment.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://t.co/42h9aR4sem

statements.text:
Nothing is binding about these empty words. Trump can spin this meaningless pledge all he wants, but we need enforceable rules on advanced AI that hold these billionaire executives accountable—before it's too late.
https://t.co/6rslaSxeCm

This is an unacceptable position from President Trump and will end in catastrophe. 

It is the government’s job to regulate industry — especially frontier AI that has the capacity to harm human beings at a massive scale. 

I urge President Trump to take this threat seriously and take real action. It’s also imperative the U.S. lead negotiations with China to develop global rules of the road on AI.
statements.quoted: Trump on giant AI companies: "They're gonna police. They're gonna police each other. They're gonna self-police. They're gonna police themselves. It's gonna work out very well." https://t.co/NoL4JlQxdR

statements.text: 68,000 people exposed. Hackers with an open-source AI tool. No country can fight this alone. The U.S. and China must cooperate on AI security now, before our financial system is next. https://t.co/JZfKqnPSn7
statements.quoted: Hackers used a Chinese AI agent to attack South Korea’s biggest banks—one of the first such AI-powered intrusions into the global financial system https://t.co/9nRHXjXdGc

statements.text:
It shouldn’t take a catastrophe for Washington to regulate AI companies. 

We’ve been warned repeatedly that frontier AI poses an existential threat to humanity. The companies themselves are preparing for it. 

Congress and the President need to act now. https://t.co/hfF4rTPR4e
statements.quoted: SCOOP: Top executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt after a catastrophic AI event. https://t.co/SC1Wur2dS0

statements.text:
I’ve heard some Members of Congress say they “don’t know enough about AI to regulate it.” That’s absurd. 

Just as we regulate airplanes, pharmaceutical drugs, cars and nuclear weapons, we need guardrails on advanced AI and we must ban artificial superintelligence - urgently. 

Anything other than that is an abdication of our responsibility to the American people. And the consequences of continued inaction will be nothing short of catastrophic.
statements.quoted: Bill Gates warns of "grim possibilities if we don't maintain control" of AI and says “over the next year we’ll move beyond self-governance… It's clear we're not doing enough.” https://t.co/VvPzd7LtdC

statements.text:
I warned Matt Buechele on That Sounds Like a Lot that Donald Trump is wrong and AI companies cannot self-regulate.

We need urgent and bipartisan AI regulation from Congress. https://t.co/HTUxlC35SO

The fact that Congress remains out of session as unauthorized AI agents are hacking major U.S. banks is INSANE. 

It’s a complete abdication of responsibility led by Mike Johnson, as he continues to take orders from a disgustingly corrupt White House.

It’s long past time for an immediate pause on advanced AI development.
statements.quoted:
SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

Several bank executives told Axios they're struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://t.co/Q3bda5In8q

statements.text: Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence.

In the wake of recent alarming revelations by leading AI experts at Anthropic, OpenAI, and other companies, we write to you as members of Congress who maintain our dedication to preserving American leadership in critical and emerging technologies, but are nonetheless deeply concerned by emerging signs of highly capable frontier Artificial Intelligence and its ramifications. As AI rapidly advances in the U.S. and around the globe, your administration must immediately initiate dialogue with allies, and also competitors and adversaries, to engage in comprehensive and urgent negotiations regarding the future of AI. These much-needed negotiations will enhance our economic competitiveness while preserving global national security for generations to come.

True global security in the untested and fast-advancing field of AI requires stability, predictability, and strategic restraint. Without deliberate multilateral mechanisms for coordinated restraint and calculated risk reduction, the race by multibillion dollar companies to deploy ever-more powerful models risks inadvertently triggering a global economic disruption, attacks on critical infrastructure, the spread of supercharged disease, dangerous military miscalculations, and other potentially devastating impacts for humanity.

We strongly urge your administration to lead a coordinated international effort to establish a global framework to guide the development of this technology and a shared vision for AI end-use — engaging our strongest allies, such as the European Union, as well as formidable global competitors, particularly the People’s Republic of China.
